skill.name: edit-article
skill.description: Helps users revise article drafts by organizing sections, confirming structure, and rewriting prose for clarity and flow.
skill.summary: Guides structured article edits with section planning and concise rewrites.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported for this prompt-only skill, so no finding verdicts are required. I reviewed SKILL.md and found no prompt injection, credential access, network behavior, filesystem behavior, or executable code. The skill is limited to article restructuring and prose revision guidance.

content.value_statement: Draft articles can lose readers when sections feel unclear or out of order. This skill guides structured revision, clearer prose, and tighter paragraphs.
actual_capabilities: Divides an article into heading-based sections before rewriting.
Checks section order against dependency flow between ideas.
Asks the user to confirm the planned section structure.
Rewrites each section for clarity, coherence, and flow.
Keeps rewritten paragraphs within a 240-character limit.
limitations: It does not fact-check claims or verify citations.
It requires an existing article draft from the user.
It focuses on prose and structure, not publication design.
It does not provide executable editing tools or document export.

use_cases.title: Improve Technical Drafts
use_cases.description: Developers can reorganize technical posts so prerequisites appear before advanced points.

use_cases.title: Prepare Newsletter Articles
use_cases.description: Editors can tighten long drafts into clearer sections with shorter paragraphs.

use_cases.title: Refine Thought Leadership
use_cases.description: Founders can improve structure and flow before publishing opinion articles.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use edit-article on this draft. Split it into sections, suggest an order, and wait for my confirmation before rewriting.

prompt_templates.title: Tighten Section Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this article for unclear section order. Explain the dependency chain between sections, then propose a better structure.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for Concision
prompt_templates.prompt: After I approve the section plan, rewrite each section for clarity. Keep every paragraph under 240 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Editorial Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this long article for structure, coherence, and flow. Preserve my core argument, but reorder sections where dependencies require it.

output_examples.input: A draft article with headings that introduce examples before explaining the core concept.
output_examples.output: The output proposes a reordered section outline, asks for confirmation, then rewrites sections with shorter paragraphs after approval.

output_examples.input: A long section with repeated points and paragraphs that are hard to scan.
output_examples.output: The rewritten section removes repeated phrasing, improves transitions, and keeps each paragraph concise.

output_examples.input: A technical article where later sections rely on ideas introduced too late.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies dependency problems and moves prerequisite explanations earlier in the article.

best_practices: Provide the full draft with all headings before asking for edits.
Review and approve the proposed section order before requesting rewrites.
State the intended audience and publishing context for better editorial choices.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent sources, quotes, or facts.
Do not skip section confirmation when the article has complex structure.
Do not use it as a grammar checker for isolated sentences.

faq.question: Can this skill edit technical articles?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for articles where ideas depend on earlier explanations.

faq.question: Does it rewrite the whole article at once?
faq.answer: It first proposes section structure and asks for confirmation before rewriting sections.

faq.question: Will it keep paragraphs short?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for paragraphs of no more than 240 characters.

faq.question: Does it fact-check the article?
faq.answer: No. It improves structure and prose, but it does not verify factual claims.

faq.question: Can I preserve my tone?
faq.answer: Yes. Include tone guidance and examples when you provide the draft.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
